title: Monitoring Forest Damage Caused by Pine Wilt Disease with Remote Sensing Technologies: A review

title: Multi-sensor geospatial modelling to address complex mangrove dieback: misattribution of chemical stressors versus physical impact
method: forensic geospatial reconstruction testing two competing causal hypotheses
sensor: Sentinel-2, lidar geomorphic model, ERA5 reanalysis

title: Evaluating the Potential of annual Sentinel-1 Composites for Bark Beetle Infestation Detection
venue: ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences

title: Previous prescribed burns saved thousands of ancient sequoias during historically unprecedented wildfires.

sensor: 3 m PlanetScope, airborne lidar, field observations
notes: Lidar contributes to mortality mapping, not to agent attribution.

title: Identification of Cypress Bark Beetle-Infested Cypress Based on LiDAR and RGB Imagery

agent: fire injury, native bark beetles including Dendroctonus brevicomis, comandra blister rust

title: Assessment of military impacts on protected areas of Ukraine using Sentinel-1 and machine learning
venue: Man and Environment Issues of Neoecology
method: baseline-relative change analysis and unsupervised classification of radar vegetation index
host: eastern Ukraine forest, species not stated
notes: Radar separates a disturbance type from background variability using a control site, not a multi-agent classifier.

title: High-Resolution Mapping, Attribution, and Carbon Loss Assessment of Forest Disturbances in China’s Critical Regions Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing
method: Bayesian model averaging over LandTrendr, CCDC and 1D-CNN, then automated driver attribution
sensor: Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Landsat 8/9, GEDI L4B lidar, FIRMS
host: Northeast China and Hengduan Mountains forest, species not stated

title: Monitoring changes of forest height in California
method: deep neural network predicting canopy height from radar and optical imagery, trained on GEDI RH98
sensor: GEDI lidar, radar and optical satellite imagery
agent: wildfire, drought, insect infestation, human activity
notes: Structure change is mapped across disturbance types but the agents are not separated.

title: Dual-Task Learning for Dead Tree Detection and Segmentation with Hybrid Self-Attention U-Nets in Aerial Imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: dual-task self-attention U-Net with watershed postprocessing for dead tree detection
accuracy_metric: relative improvement in instance segmentation accuracy
notes: Mortality detection with no agent label.

title: Remote Sensing Technology for Observing Tree Mortality and Its Influences on Carbon–Water Dynamics
method: systematic literature and bibliometric review
notes: Review of remote sensing for tree mortality, 1998 to mid-2024.

title: Post-fire regeneration dynamics of heterogeneous Mediterranean ecosystems using Landsat and ALS data.
method: random forest relating ALS structure to Landsat indices, BART for drivers
notes: Structure used for recovery assessment, single disturbance type.

title: Kennaugh Elements Allow Early Detection of Bark Beetle Infestation in Temperate Forests Using Sentinel-1 Data
method: Multi-SAR time series with Kennaugh element decomposition, random forest
host: Bavarian Forest National Park, spruce implied, not stated
notes: Radar for early detection of one insect agent. No between-agent discrimination.

title: Deep learning interpretability for understanding forest disturbance driver classification from Sentinel-1 and -2 data
method: deep learning fusion models for disturbance driver classification, six XAI methods applied
agent: tropical forest disturbance drivers, classes not enumerated in abstract
notes: Driver attribution with radar contributing. Drivers are land-use classes, not two insects.

title: Mapping Windthrow Risk in Pinus radiata Plantations Using Multi-Temporal LiDAR and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Cyclone Gabrielle, New Zealand
method: random forest on repeat lidar, optical and climate surfaces, 9713 plots
sensor: repeat regional airborne lidar, optical imagery
validation_design: 50 iterations of 80/20 train and test splits
notes: Lidar structure for windthrow, a single abiotic agent.

title: Forest attribute maps: a support for small area estimation of forest disturbances
method: small area estimation using forest attribute maps from NFI and remote sensing
notes: Impact quantification, not agent attribution.

title: Mangrove Damage and Early-Stage Canopy Recovery Following Hurricane Roslyn in Marismas Nacionales, Mexico
method: time series of Combined Mangrove Recognition Index and canopy height model change
notes: Structure for damage and recovery, single agent.

title: Functional Traits From Imaging Spectroscopy Inform Patterns of Forest Mortality During Sierra Nevada Drought
method: trait-mortality relationships from imaging spectroscopy with climate, topography, canopy structure
sensor: AVIRIS-Classic imaging spectrometer, canopy structure data
agent: drought and insect outbreak, not separated
validation_design: two independently derived mortality datasets compared
notes: Drought and insect drivers are treated jointly rather than separated.

title: Estimation of Forest Structure and Fuel Change Across Mountain Pine Beetle – Attacked Forests Using Mobile and RPAS – Based LiDAR
method: lidar metrics from point clouds used to model fuel components after attack
notes: Structure quantifies consequences of one insect agent, not agent identity.

title: Dual Polarimetric Radar Vegetation Index for monitoring forest moisture stress using time series of Sentinel‐1 SAR data
method: monthly median deviations of a dual polarimetric radar vegetation index
notes: First use of DpRVI for drought effects in forests per the abstract. Abiotic agent only.

title: Aboveground Biomass and Tree Mortality Revealed Through Multi-Scale LiDAR Analysis
method: comparison of GEDI-simulated waveforms, UAV grid metrics and individual tree detection for AGB and mortality
sensor: airborne lidar, UAV lidar, GEDI simulation
notes: Mortality prediction from structure with no agent label.

title: Spatial Diffusion Characteristics of Pine Wilt Disease at the Forest Stand Scale and Prediction of Individual Tree Mortality Risk
method: spatiotemporal diffusion reconstruction and tree-level mortality risk model
sensor: UAV multispectral (23 phases), airborne lidar, field survey
accuracy_value: 50% of transmission events within 17.2 m, spatial autocorrelation range about 28 m
notes: Single agent. Lidar supports stand structure, not agent identification.

title: Multi-Dimensional Estimation of Leaf Loss Rate from Larch Caterpillar Under Insect Pest Stress Using UAV-Based Multi-Source Remote Sensing
method: recursive feature elimination then random forest regression and CNN regression for leaf loss rate
notes: Lidar indices contribute to severity estimation for one insect agent.

title: The Mapping and Analysis of the Infrequent, Large‐Scale Blowdown Event in the Colorado Front Range
method: change vector analysis of pre and post-event imagery, tunable thresholds
host: Colorado Front Range forest, species not stated
validation_design: compared against Global Forest Change data
accuracy_metric: true positive versus false positive rates
notes: Single agent mapping with a tunable error trade-off.

title: Differentiating Acute and Chronic Stress in Norway Spruce using Hyperspectral and Thermal Remote Sensing in Experimental Plots
venue: The International Archives of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
method: experimental plots with edge exposure and roofing, spectral and thermal comparison
sensor: UAV and aircraft hyperspectral and thermal
agent: acute thermal stress versus chronic drought stress
validation_design: experimental controls, no classifier accuracy reported
notes: Close analogue in structure of the problem: two stressors separated on one host. Both stressors are abiotic, so it does not refute the two-insect claim.

title: Understanding defoliation of Pinus plantations in the Mediterranean mountains using tree segmentation and ALS time series.
method: tree segmentation, height and defoliation from ALS time series using kNN, random forest and neural networks
agent: drought and pest outbreak, described as climatic-driven defoliation
notes: Structure used to grade defoliation severity. Agents are not separated.

title: Detekcja pojedynczych martwych świerków w Puszczy Białowieskiej na podstawie integracji danych satelitarnych z danymi lotniczego skanowania laserowego
method: integration of satellite imagery with airborne laser scanning to detect individual dead trees
notes: Polish-language paper, Bialowieza Forest. Single agent.

title: Terrestrial lidar scanning provides efficient measurements of fire-caused crown scorch in longleaf pine
method: prediction of crown scorch from terrestrial lidar return intensity, 253 trees
notes: Lidar intensity as a proxy for crown injury, single agent.

title: Severely disturbed forests in Central Europe retain robust recovery capacity but face resilience loss due to spatial homogenization
method: integration of optical and SAR with UAV imagery and vegetation height models to map disturbance and recovery
sensor: optical satellite, SAR, UAV imagery, vegetation height models
agent: spruce bark beetle outbreak and salvage logging
accuracy_value: 30.8% of initial forest area disturbed 2018 to 2024
notes: Beetle and salvage logging are treated as a compound sequence, not separated as competing agents.

title: Early detection of Dendrolimus species infestations: integrating UAV hyperspectral and LiDAR data
method: SPA, ISIC and ISIC-SPA feature selection with random forest on combined hyperspectral and lidar features
notes: Explicitly argues canopy structure is underexplored for early detection and adds lidar to spectra. Detection of infestation stage, not discrimination between Dendrolimus species. Flagged for full-text check.

title: Canopy height and its spatial heterogeneity predominantly determine damages to tropical forests by major hurricanes, with a mitigating legacy effect of drought
method: spatial error models of canopy height reduction on pre-hurricane canopy properties
notes: Structure predicts damage severity from one agent.

title: Detection of the sharp-toothed bark-beetle infection using UAV multispectral and LiDAR data in Scots pine forest of Kampinoski National Park, Poland
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: UAV lidar to isolate the crown layer, vegetation indices, random forest classification
agent: sharp-toothed bark beetle (Ips acuminatus, described as Xylophagos beetle)
notes: Lidar used to delimit crowns; discrimination is spectral. Two-class healthy versus infested, one agent.

title: Single tree health monitoring using uav-based lidar data
method: UAV lidar metrics for tree health status
notes: Conference abstract only. Structure-only health assessment, no agent.

title: Unprecedented tropical cyclone in temperate-boreal ecotone drives declines in emergent conifers and canopy complexity.
method: analysis of fallen tree dimensions from drone orthophotographs across four sites
host: Abies holophylla, Pinus koraiensis and broadleaves
notes: Single agent, species-differential vulnerability.

title: Measuring Changes in Forest Carbon Stocks using an IPCC-Compliant Method with a Competition-Index-Based Volumetric Model and Multi-temporal Airborne Laser Scanning Data
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: IPCC-compliant carbon stock estimation with a competition-index volumetric model on multitemporal ALS
notes: Structure quantifies carbon consequence of disturbance, agents not separated.

title: Using airborne LiDAR to quantify changes in forest structure following an ice storm disturbance and subsequent salvage logging
method: leaf area density profiles and voxel-based biomass loss from multitemporal high-density ALS, validated against field data
agent: ice storm and subsequent salvage logging
host: Picea abies, Abies alba, Fagus sylvatica
notes: Two disturbance types quantified, but they are abiotic damage and harvest, and they differ in timing and pattern.

title: Effectiveness of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle-Based LiDAR for Assessing the Impact of Catastrophic Windstorm Events on Timberland
method: random forest, maximum likelihood and decision tree classification of windstorm damage with and without a lidar canopy height model
support: stand, ten stands of 10 to 20 acres
notes: Directly quantifies the gain from adding a lidar canopy height model to imagery for damage classification. Single agent class.

title: Quantifying Forest Structural and Functional Responses to Fire Severity Using Multi-Source Remotely Sensed Data
method: correlation and LOESS regression of structural change against burn severity indices
sensor: pre and post-fire airborne lidar, Landsat dNBR
notes: Lidar structure related to a spectral severity index for one agent.

title: A large net carbon loss attributed to anthropogenic and natural disturbances in the Amazon Arc of Deforestation
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
method: partitioning of aboveground carbon loss between clearing, logging and fire using airborne laser scanning
accuracy_metric: area affected and net carbon flux
accuracy_value: degradation 3.5% of surveyed area versus 0.7% cleared; net loss -90.5 +/- 16.6 Tg C per year 2016 to 2018
notes: Partitions loss between anthropogenic and natural causes. Agents are logging, fire and clearing, not insects.

title: Gap expansion is the dominant driver of canopy openings in a temperate mountain forest landscape
method: canopy height change analysis at 1 m resolution across three repeat lidar acquisitions, 11,331 gaps
notes: Repeat lidar for gap dynamics. No agent labels.

title: Mapping the natural disturbance risk to protective forests across the European Alps.
method: ensemble models combining satellite disturbance history with spaceborne lidar structure to map hazard, exposure and vulnerability
sensor: Landsat-based disturbance maps 1986 to 2020, GEDI spaceborne lidar
agent: windthrow, bark beetle outbreak, forest fire
notes: Uses lidar structure alongside three named agents, but for risk mapping, not for deciding which agent caused an observed damage patch.

title: Post-Logging Canopy Gap Dynamics and Forest Regeneration Assessed Using Airborne LiDAR Time Series in the Brazilian Amazon with Attribution to Gap Types and Origins
method: airborne lidar time series gap detection with attribution of gaps to types and origins
agent: selective logging and natural gap formation
notes: Attribution of gaps to origin using lidar structure alone. Origins are logging versus natural, not two insects.

title: Identification of Larch Caterpillar Infestation Severity Based on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Multispectral and LiDAR Features
method: ANOVA feature selection then random forest and support vector machine severity classification
sensor: UAV multispectral, UAV lidar, ground measurements
accuracy_metric: not stated in abstract, feature importance reported
accuracy_value: NDGI and the 25% height percentile were the most sensitive features
notes: A lidar height percentile is among the two most sensitive features for insect damage severity. Single agent, severity grading.

title: Submonthly Assessment of Temperate Forest Clear-Cuts in Mainland France
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
method: radar change ratio adapted from a tropical near real-time forest loss method
host: French temperate broadleaf and conifer forest
notes: Radar detects harvest, an agent with a sharp and complete canopy signal.

title: Tall Bornean forests experience higher canopy disturbance rates than those in the eastern Amazon or Guiana shield
method: framework for disturbance and recovery analysis in lidar time series at 1 m resolution
host: old-growth tropical forest, Borneo, Amazon, Guiana shield
notes: Structure-only disturbance rates, no agent attribution.

title: Mapping recent timber harvest activity in a temperate forest using single date airborne LiDAR surveys and machine learning: lessons for conservation planning
method: XGBoost on single-campaign airborne lidar to map recent harvest
agent: timber harvest, including shelterwood, overstory removal and clearcut
notes: Single-date structure distinguishes harvest intensity classes. The classes are harvest types, not agents.

title: Evaluating the potential for continuous update of enhanced forest inventory attributes using optical satellite data
venue: Forestry: An International Journal of Forest Research
method: optical time series used to update an ALS-derived enhanced forest inventory at two-week intervals
sensor: optical satellite time series, airborne laser scanning
notes: Inventory updating rather than agent attribution.

title: Predictive Model for Bark Beetle Outbreaks in European Forests
method: random forest regression and comparison of machine learning architectures for outbreak probability
sensor: environmental and climatic predictors, remote sensing derived
notes: Risk prediction for one agent.

title: Forest Disturbance Detection via Self-Supervised and Transfer Learning With Sentinel-1&2 Images
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
method: self-supervised knowledge distillation with transfer learning and deep change vector analysis
notes: Two abiotic agents handled as two separate use cases, not as competing classes in one classifier.

title: Sensitivity of Sentinel-1 Backscatter to Management-Related Disturbances in Temperate Forests
method: analysis of dense C-band backscatter against experimentally imposed disturbance intensities at 14 sites
validation_design: 14 experimental sites with controlled removal levels
notes: Rare experimental control on disturbance intensity for a radar sensitivity study.

title: DIAMANTE: A data-centric semantic segmentation approach to map tree dieback induced by bark beetle infestations via satellite images
venue: Journal of Intelligence and Information Systems
method: data-centric semantic segmentation of tree dieback
notes: Single agent segmentation.

title: Remote Sensing of Forests in Bavaria: A Review
method: systematic literature review, 146 articles 2008 to 2023
notes: Notes that 88 of 146 studies were in the Bavarian Forest National Park, a concentration worth citing on generalisability.

title: Early spectral dynamics are indicative of distinct growth patterns in post‐wildfire forests
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
method: space-for-time substitution linking early post-fire spectral dynamics to RPAS lidar structure
sensor: RPAS lidar, optical satellite time series
notes: Links spectral trajectory to structural outcome for one agent.

title: Mapping Windthrow Severity as Change in Canopy Cover in a Temperate Eucalypt Forest
method: training on 455 plots of aerial-image canopy cover, mapping percentage canopy cover change
validation_design: randomly selected plots in disturbed and undisturbed areas
notes: Severity as canopy cover change, single agent.

title: EWMACD Algorithm in Early Detection of Defoliation Caused by Dendrolimus tabulaeformis Tsai et Liu
method: EWMACD change detection on fused Sentinel-2 and downscaled Landsat-8 time series
sensor: Sentinel-2, Landsat-8 downscaled to 10 m by deep learning
notes: Early detection of one defoliator.

title: Canopy Structural Changes in Black Pine Trees Affected by Pine Processionary Moth Using Drone-Derived Data
method: bitemporal high-density drone lidar, manual crown delineation compared with lidar methods, parametric statistics on canopy metrics
notes: One of the few studies that measures canopy structural change caused by an insect defoliator directly from lidar. Contrasts defoliated with non-defoliated trees of one host, but only one insect agent is present.

title: Feasibility study of forest wood-boring pest detection base on hyperspectral LiDAR
method: hyperspectral lidar echo intensity ratio then support vector machine on trunk bark
notes: Active lidar targeting the trunk rather than the canopy, aimed at detecting attack before defoliation. Single agent.

title: Exploring the Detection of Bark Beetle Attacks in Norway Spruce Forests in Sentinel-1 Image Time Series
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: analysis of VV and VH backscatter distributions before and after attack, automatic detection method
validation_design: tested on the same polygons used for reference
notes: Tested on the same polygons from which the reference was drawn, so the figure is close to resubstitution.

title: Ant Nest Detection Using Underground P-Band TomoSAR
method: electromagnetic simulation of nest signatures then drone-borne P-band tomographic SAR with a convolutional network
notes: Radar detects the insect agent itself rather than its canopy damage, by imaging underground nests. Distinctive but single agent.

title: Assessing the burn severity of wildfires by incorporating vegetation structure information
method: polarimetric decomposition features and PCA into a random forest predicting composite burn index
notes: Explicitly argues vegetation structure information is underused in severity assessment, and supplies it from polarimetry.

title: Investigating the potential of ICEYE-SAR data in storm damage detection in a coniferous forest with rugged terrain
method: unsupervised change detection combining wavelet transform with adaptive thresholds at four spatial scales
notes: Very high resolution SAR for structural damage, single agent.

title: Multi-Band Scattering Characteristics of Miniature Masson Pine Canopy Based on Microwave Anechoic Chamber Measurement
method: controlled anechoic chamber backscatter measurement of canopy scenes at four defoliation densities
sensor: C-, X- and Ku-band microwave, ground-based
accuracy_value: not extracted, reported by band and angle
notes: Direct physical evidence on which canopy components drive backscatter at different defoliation levels. Useful mechanistic citation for a radar-structure hypothesis.

title: The Significance of Tree Height as a Predictor of Tree Mortality during Bark Beetle Outbreaks in a Small Catchment
method: machine learning variable importance on tree category time series from aerial images with lidar heights
sensor: aerial imagery at 20 cm, terrestrial lidar campaigns 2010 and 2011
accuracy_value: tree height was the most influential variable in each year
notes: Direct evidence that a structural variable predicts which trees an insect kills. Single agent.

title: Discriminating between Biotic and Abiotic Stress in Poplar Forests Using Hyperspectral and LiDAR Data
method: partial least squares VIP variable selection then PLS-SVM, four models: healthy, drought, ALB, and four-class
agent: Asian longhorned beetle and drought, singly and combined
support: individual tree, 325 poplars across four 50 x 50 m plots
validation_design: train and test split 7 to 3 with 10-fold cross-validation, not spatially blocked
class_balance_reported: yes: 66 healthy, 75 ALB only, 80 drought only, 104 combined
accuracy_metric: overall accuracy, kappa, producer's and user's accuracy from confusion matrices
accuracy_value: four-class OA 78.79%; drought OA 94.85% K 0.90; ALB OA 80.81% K 0.62; healthy 94.79%; ALB producer's accuracy 86.96% well watered versus 79.41% water deficient
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ3, full text read. Zhou et al. 2024. Host held constant (Populus gansuensis) and two agents separated with lidar metrics among the top predictors. Discussion states verbatim: 'Unlike previous studies, in this experiment, LiDAR metrics effectively detect forest pest.' A lidar variable, Height_99th/Tree Height, is among the five most important for the ALB model. One agent is abiotic, so the two-insect wording survives; the claim that structure has never been used to identify which agent caused damage does not.

title: Detection of snow disturbances in boreal forests using unitemporal airborne lidar data and aerial images
venue: Forestry: An International Journal of Forest Research

class_balance_reported: yes, 81 healthy versus 128 disturbed plots stated
notes: Single-date lidar detects a structural signature of one abiotic agent at tree level. Motivates the work by the raised risk of subsequent insect outbreak.

title: Forest Harvest Detection Using SAR Coherence Time Series: A Case Study of Bark Beetle Outbreak in the Czech Republic
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: SAR interferometric coherence time series compared with annual harvest records
agent: bark beetle outbreak followed by salvage harvest
validation_design: visual comparison with ground truth harvest data
notes: Coherence responds to salvage removal rather than to the beetle attack itself.

title: Unmanned Ground Vehicle for Identifying Trees Infested with Bark Beetles
method: computer vision classification of resin stains on bark from an autonomous ground vehicle
sensor: ground vehicle camera, rotating lidar for navigation only
notes: Ground-level early indicator, offered as a contrast to aerial monitoring which the authors say detects only advanced stages.

title: Tracking Spatial and Temporal Variation in Forest Canopy Conditions in the Boreal Forest of Alaska Using Lidar Data
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: canopy height model differencing and canopy cover change 2017 to 2023
agent: not stated, mortality in white spruce
validation_design: comparison with 37 years of ground data
accuracy_value: 84% of trees showed height variation corresponding with ground canopy change
notes: Structure detects mortality without identifying its cause.

title: UAV-based reference data for the prediction of fractional cover of standing deadwood from Sentinel time series
venue: ISPRS Open Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
method: CNN semantic segmentation of dead crowns on UAV orthomosaics to generate reference data for Sentinel time series regression
sensor: UAV RGB at under 4 cm, Sentinel time series
agent: tree mortality including drought, windthrow, harvest, wildfire
notes: Notes that non-stand-replacing mortality is the harder case, which is the regime the adelgid problem sits in.

title: Assessing Combinations of Landsat, Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-1 Time series for Detecting Bark Beetle Infestations
method: Bayesian conditional probability and random forest regression on index time series, five sensor configurations compared
host: Norway spruce, Bavarian Forest National Park

accuracy_value: Sentinel-2 0.93; Landsat 0.89; Landsat plus Sentinel-2 0.87; all three combined 0.67; Sentinel-1 alone 0.62
