title: Potential of Sentinel-1 SAR to Assess Damage in Drought-Affected Temperate Deciduous Broadleaf Forests
method: temporal-only time series filtering of radiometric and polarimetric indices, anomaly analysis
support: 10 m by 10 m, described as single-tree scale
notes: Radar sensitivity to foliage loss from an abiotic agent.

title: Delineating and Reconstructing 3D Forest Fuel Components and Volumes with Terrestrial Laser Scanning
method: transformer-based deep learning classification of TLS point clouds into eight fuel classes with quantitative structural models
sensor: terrestrial laser scanning, twelve plot scans
notes: Structural consequence of one insect agent, for fuel modelling.

title: Estimating Structural Damage to Mangrove Forests Using Airborne Lidar Imagery: Case Study of Damage Induced by the 2017 Hurricane Irma to Mangroves in the Florida Everglades, USA
method: lidar structural change with field data to model aboveground necromass
notes: Single agent, structural damage quantification.

title: Estimating Individual Tree Mortality in the Sierra Nevada Using Lidar and Multispectral Reflectance Data
method: lidar crown delineation then multispectral mortality mapping over more than one million trees
notes: Lidar supplies crown geometry; mortality itself is detected spectrally.

title: Post-Hurricane Damage Severity Classification at the Individual Tree Level Using Terrestrial Laser Scanning and Deep Learning
method: convolutional neural networks on 2D images rendered from TLS point clouds, six architectures compared
notes: States that no prior study had combined TLS with deep learning for hurricane damage at individual tree level. Damage severity classes, one agent.

title: Airborne laser scanning reveals uniform responses of forest structure to moose (Alces alces) across the boreal forest biome
method: airborne laser scanning across 100 paired exclosure and control plots
notes: Rare case of structure isolating a biotic herbivory agent under experimental control. The agent is a vertebrate browser, not an insect.

title: Predicting snow damage in conifer forests using a mechanistic snow damage model and high-resolution snow accumulation data
method: mechanistic critical snow load model driven by numerical weather prediction, validated on lidar-derived breakage
sensor: pre and post-damage airborne laser scanning
accuracy_metric: damage versus no-damage class separation, described as satisfactory
notes: Very large tree-level reference set derived from repeat ALS.

title: The 30-year impact of post-windthrow management on the forest regeneration process in northern Japan
method: quantification of structural recovery from aerial photographs and lidar over 30 years
notes: Disturbance and management effects on structural recovery.

title: Seeing the Disturbed Forest for the Trees: Remote Sensing Is Underutilized to Quantify Critical Zone Response to Unprecedented Disturbance
method: synthesis and perspective on integrating remote sensing platforms for disturbance response
notes: Argues that integrating disturbance measures across sensing platforms is complex and underused.

title: Disturbance of Wind Damage and Insect Outbreaks in the Old-Growth Forest of Changbai Mountain, Northeast China
method: combination of low-frequency optical disturbance products with high-frequency meteorological data to identify agent and timing
notes: Explicit two-agent attribution. Abstract states verbatim that wind damage and insect outbreaks are two main forest disturbance agents. Wind and insect differ in timing and pattern, so this is the standard contrast, not two insects on one host.

title: Size Estimation of Ant Nests in Industrial Forest by P-Band SAR Tomography
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: drone-borne P-band SAR tomography with a convolutional neural network estimating nest size
notes: Radar imaging of the insect's subsurface structure rather than of canopy damage.

title: Old-Growth Forests in Urban Nature Reserves: Balancing Risks for Visitors and Biodiversity Protection in Warsaw, Poland
method: airborne laser scanning defoliation detection compared with storm damage occurrence
agent: crown defoliation of unstated cause, then Storm Eunice 2022
notes: Structural condition before an event predicts which trees the event damages.

title: Mapping temperate forest stands using mobile terrestrial LiDAR shows the influence of forest management regimes on tree mortality
method: mobile terrestrial lidar rapid 3D mapping of stands to compare mortality across management regimes
notes: States that tree death is often caused by accumulation and interaction of stressors, which is the general obstacle to single-agent attribution.

title: Tree Condition and Analysis Program – Detecting Forest Disturbance at the Tree Level across the Contiguous United States with High Resolution Imagery
method: open-source operational system classifying tree crown condition as healthy or damaged
sensor: NAIP high-resolution airborne imagery and lidar
agent: bark beetle, emerald ash borer, hemlock woolly adelgid, drought, one per site
validation_design: four study sites, design not stated
notes: Directly relevant to RQ1: hemlock woolly adelgid mortality in Pennsylvania is one of the four demonstrations. Each agent occupies a separate site with a separate host, so no agent is discriminated from another.

title: Estimating the extent of selective timber harvesting in private native eucalypt forests with multi-temporal lidar
method: design-based sampling of multi-temporal lidar transects to map harvest-related canopy change
host: private native eucalypt forest, New South Wales
notes: Design-based inference from lidar samples, a useful precedent for sampling design.

title: Semi-Supervised Deep Learning Representations in Earth Observation Based Forest Management
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: self-supervised deep learning representations, deep change vector analysis and UNet-based regression
notes: Two abiotic agents as separate mapping tasks.

title: Windthrows Detection With Satellite Remote Sensing Data: A Comparison Among Sentinel-2, Planet, And Cosmo Sky-Med Data
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: comparison of active and passive sensors for windthrow detection across acquisition seasons
notes: Direct optical versus radar comparison for one agent.

title: Comparison of Tower-Based and Satellite L- and C-Band Radar Backscatter from a Boreal Forest
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: comparison of tower-based tomographic radar with spaceborne SAR over a fixed forest site
sensor: BorealScat tower radar L- and C-band, Sentinel-1, ALOS-2 PALSAR-2
agent: bark beetle infestation causing tree deaths
accuracy_value: agreement within 0.9 dB C-band and 0.6 dB L-band for healthy forest; Sentinel-1 backscatter insensitive to tree deaths while tower-based tomographic backscatter showed clear variation
notes: Load-bearing negative result. Spaceborne C-band did not register beetle-caused mortality that tomographic ground radar did register, which bounds what a satellite SAR predictor can be expected to carry.

title: Sensitivity Testing Analysis of Airborne Hyperspectral Lidar Signals for Monitoring Insects and Diseases Based on 3d Radiative Transfer Model
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: 3D radiative transfer simulation (LESS) of airborne hyperspectral lidar point clouds under defined damage scenarios
sensor: simulated airborne hyperspectral lidar, simulated hyperspectral imagery, TLS for scene construction
agent: forest insects and diseases, simulated stress levels
notes: Targets damage in the lower canopy, where passive imagery cannot see, using an active hyperspectral lidar.

title: A First Assessment of Canopy Cover Loss in Germany's Forests after the 2018-2020 Drought Years
method: disturbance index from tasseled cap components with monthly quantile composites and anomalies against a 2017 reference
sensor: Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 dense time series
agent: drought with cascading bark beetle infestation
accuracy_value: 501,000 ha lost in Germany January 2018 to April 2021
notes: Drought and beetle are described as a cascade and are not separated.

title: Integrating GEDI and Landsat: Spaceborne Lidar and Four Decades of Optical Imagery for the Analysis of Forest Disturbances and Biomass Changes in Italy
method: Landsat disturbance mapping with GEDI biomass assessed against ALS
sensor: Landsat 1985 to 2019, GEDI spaceborne lidar, ALS reference
accuracy_value: harvest omission error 29% in 2012 to 65% in 2001; r2 0.75 between GEDI and ALS biomass density
notes: Quantifies how much disturbance an optical record misses, useful for bounding label quality.

title: Mapping a European Spruce Bark Beetle Outbreak Using Sentinel-2 Remote Sensing Data
method: support vector machine on vegetation indices, with lidar used for automatic crown delineation and species classification
notes: Lidar contributes crown geometry and species, not the infestation signal.

title: Forest disturbance and growth processes are reflected in the geographical distribution of large canopy gaps across the Brazilian Amazon
method: power-law characterisation of canopy gap size distributions across 650 randomly distributed lidar transects
agent: human disturbance and natural mortality processes
accuracy_value: not extracted, reported as regional variation in alpha
notes: Gap size distribution as a structural fingerprint of disturbance regime. It separates regimes, not individual events.

title: Mapping tree mortality rate in a tropical moist forest using multi-temporal LiDAR
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: gap dynamics index from successive canopy height models compared with field mortality rates
validation_design: comparison with field-measured mortality on permanent plots
notes: Repeat lidar mortality rates validated against permanent plots.

title: A Computationally Efficient Method for Updating Fuel Inputs for Wildfire Behavior Models Using Sentinel Imagery and Random Forest Classification
method: random forest classifier trained on radar, multispectral, land cover and tree mortality survey data to update fuel inputs
agent: tree mortality of unstated agent, then wildfire
notes: Uses an operational mortality survey as a training label source, the same design pattern as this project.

title: Assessing Forest Vitality and Forest Structure Using 3D Data: A Case Study From the Hainich National Park, Germany
venue: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
method: box-dimension structural complexity differenced between summer and winter scans to quantify vitality
agent: not stated, crown defoliation and branch dieback
notes: Structure-only vitality metric that captures branch dieback as well as defoliation. Directly relevant to a structural-signature hypothesis.

title: Health assessment of plantations based on LiDAR canopy spatial structure parameters
method: forest health indicators built from lidar canopy spatial structure parameters (Weibull alpha, VCI, sdCC, H99, cvLAD)
host: Robinia pseudoacacia plantation, Yellow River Delta
notes: Structure-only health grading built precisely because a spectral canopy vigour grade did not correlate with field biomass.

title: Quantifying Post-Fire Changes in the Aboveground Biomass of an Amazonian Forest Based on Field and Remote Sensing Data
method: random forest models of post-fire biomass loss using spectral change indices with permanent plot measurements
notes: Links canopy structural damage to spectral change over time for one agent.

title: Assessment of defoliation and subsequent growth losses caused by Lymantria dispar using terrestrial laser scanning (TLS)
method: three terrestrial laser scanning surveys before, during and after outbreak, tracking foliation and growth at individual tree level
host: oak and mixed oak forest, Germany
validation_design: large-scale field experiment with two defoliation risk levels
notes: Direct evidence that lidar structure tracks insect defoliation and subsequent growth loss at tree level. One insect agent, experimentally contrasted risk levels.

title: Identifying Conifer Tree vs. Deciduous Shrub and Tree Regeneration Trajectories in a Space-for-Time Boreal Peatland Fire Chronosequence Using Multispectral Lidar
method: lidar point cloud metrics with multispectral lidar to separate conifer from deciduous regeneration in a fire chronosequence
notes: Multispectral lidar discriminates vegetation type, not disturbance agent.

title: Monitoring Damage Caused by Pantana phyllostachysae Chao to Moso Bamboo Forests Using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 Images
method: XGBoost models on combined optical and radar features, single-date and multi-date variants
accuracy_value: single-date model using October imagery outperformed the alternatives
notes: The confound is directly analogous to this project's: off-year bamboo looks spectrally like damaged on-year bamboo, so a non-agent factor mimics the damage class.

title: Unexpected resilience in relict Abies pinsapo Boiss forests to dieback and mortality induced by climate change
method: dynamic factor analysis on end-of-dry-season NDVI time series with orthoimage and field survey of canopy structure
notes: 36-year record of decline in a relict fir, a useful analogue for a slow non-stand-replacing signal.

title: Multi-Source Mapping of Forest Susceptibility to Spruce Budworm Defoliation Based on Stand Age and Composition across a Complex Landscape in Maine, USA
method: random forest and multi-layer perceptron mapping of host species and stand impact type from radar, optical and site variables
sensor: Sentinel-1 C-band SAR, PALSAR L-band SAR, Sentinel-2
host: Picea sp. and Abies balsamea, Maine
accuracy_value: 83.4% for the best model using site variables and Sentinel-2
notes: Radar is tested alongside optical for host mapping; the best model came from optical plus terrain, not radar.

title: A comparison of radar and optical remote sensing to detect cyclone-induced canopy disturbance in two subtropical forest landscapes
method: comparison of change in two optical indices against three radar metrics for four cyclone events at two sites
host: subtropical forest, Taiwan and Puerto Rico
notes: Head-to-head radar versus optical for one agent across two independent landscapes.

title: SAR Polarimetric Phase Differences in Wetlands: Information and Mis-Information
method: physical backscatter model of an emergent cylinder over a water plane with polarimetric RADARSAT-2 observations
agent: tree mortality in swamps, cause not stated
notes: Mechanistic radar work showing co-polarised phase difference responds to standing dead trunks. Relevant to whether radar can carry a structural signature of mortality.

title: Multi-sensor remote sensing for drought characterization: current status, opportunities and a roadmap for the future
method: systematic review of multi-sensor remote sensing drought studies
notes: Reference point for the abiotic competitor agent in any attribution design.

title: Early detection of forest stress from European spruce bark beetle attack, and a new vegetation index: Normalized distance red & SWIR (NDRS)
method: comparison of radar and spectral signals of healthy versus stressed trees across a full vegetation season, and a new index NDRS
notes: Tests radar and spectral signals side by side across green-attack through late-stage infestation. A key precedent for a radar predictor in an insect attribution design.

title: Large-scale variations in the dynamics of Amazon forest canopy gaps from airborne lidar data and opportunities for tree mortality estimates
method: gap delineation by fixed and relative height methods on five multitemporal and 610 single-date lidar datasets, generalized linear models of drivers
support: gap object, 181 field plots for cross-reference
validation_design: cross-related to mortality estimates from 181 field plots
notes: Large-sample evidence that static gap structure informs about dynamic mortality.

title: Spruce budworm tree host species distribution and abundance mapping using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery
method: random forest on 191 variables from multi-temporal radar, optical and site data to map host species distribution and abundance
host: Picea sp. and Abies balsamea, New Brunswick
accuracy_value: Sentinel-2 multi-temporal single spectral bands performed best
notes: Radar tested as a host-mapping predictor rather than a damage predictor.

title: SAR data for tropical forest disturbance alerts in French Guiana: Benefit over optical imagery
method: SAR-based disturbance alert system compared against optical alerts
agent: gold mining, smallholder agriculture, forest exploitation
notes: Quantifies the benefit of radar over optical for small disturbances under persistent cloud.

title: Tracking the Rates and Mechanisms of Canopy Damage and Recovery Following Hurricane Maria Using Multitemporal Lidar Data
method: canopy height change from lidar acquired before and twice after the storm along an elevational gradient
accuracy_metric: proportion of area losing canopy height
accuracy_value: 73% of the study area lost at least 1 m of canopy height, mean -7.1 m; only 13.5% fell to 2 m or below
notes: Structural damage magnitude for one agent, with an explicit recovery trajectory.

title: Instance segmentation of fallen trees in aerial color infrared imagery using active multi-contour evolution with fully convolutional network-based intensity priors
venue: Isprs Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
method: active multi-contour evolution over fully convolutional network semantic segmentation to segment individual fallen stems
agent: bark beetle infestation causing stem fall
validation_design: three real-world scenes of varying complexity
notes: Individual-stem instance segmentation of the structural end state of an insect outbreak.

title: Continuous Detection of Forest Loss in Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia Using Sentinel-1 Data
method: shadow-based forest loss detection from radar, weekly maps over 750,000 km2
validation_design: estimated accuracies with a stated minimum mapping unit
accuracy_value: user's accuracy 0.95 disturbance and 0.99 intact; producer's accuracy 0.90 disturbance and 0.99 intact
notes: Best-documented radar disturbance accuracies in the set, but the class is loss, not agent.

title: Multisensor Data Fusion for Improved Segmentation of Individual Tree Crowns in Dense Tropical Forests
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
method: ALS point cloud clustering combined with a spectral deep learning model for crown segmentation, then repeat-survey mortality mapping
sensor: airborne laser scanning, multispectral and hyperspectral
validation_design: manually segmented reference crowns, congruence threshold 0.5
notes: Fusing structure with spectra improved crown segmentation over structure alone, which bounds mortality tracking accuracy.

title: Tracking the temporal dynamics of insect defoliation by high‐resolution radar satellite data
method: canopy development index from the ratio of backscatter intensity between two polarisations, validated against optical and terrestrial measurements
agent: gypsy moth (Lymantria dispar), densities experimentally manipulated
validation_design: replicated field experiment manipulating insect densities, radar validated against optical and terrestrial data
notes: The strongest radar-and-insect record in the set. Radar tracks the defoliation-refoliation trajectory of one insect under experimental density manipulation. Still one agent, so it does not attribute between agents.

title: Mapping Boreal Forest Spruce Beetle Health Status at the Individual Crown Scale Using Fused Spectral and Structural Data
method: fusion of UAV multispectral with structure-from-motion point clouds and G-LiHT hyperspectral and lidar, discriminating three health statuses
sensor: UAV multispectral 6 cm plus SfM point cloud, G-LiHT hyperspectral and lidar
notes: Three-class health status, non-infested, green attack and dead, from fused spectral and structural data. Closest published design to a structure-plus-spectra classifier on one host, but the classes are attack stages of one agent, not two agents.

title: Detection of Forest Windstorm Damages with Multitemporal SAR Data - A Case Study: Finland
method: three candidate methods for localising damage, assessing severity and estimating damaged area from multitemporal SAR
notes: States the core confusion problem for radar: severe windthrow can affect backscatter similarly to clear cutting, while small damage can raise neighbouring backscatter. That is a direct warning about radar-based agent attribution.

title: Measuring the Contribution of Leaves to the Structural Complexity of Urban Tree Crowns with Terrestrial Laser Scanning
method: box-dimension from TLS point clouds in leaf-on and leaf-off conditions, plus algorithmic defoliation of leaf-on clouds
host: Gleditsia triacanthos, Quercus macrocarpa, Metasequoia glyptostroboides, 45 trees on a university campus
validation_design: paired leaf-on and leaf-off scans of the same trees
accuracy_value: leaf-on box-dimension significantly greater than leaf-off across all species
notes: Mechanistic evidence that foliage loss changes a lidar structural complexity metric. Trees are urban campus specimens, not stand-grown.

title: Impact of a tropical forest blowdown on aboveground carbon balance
method: ultra-high-density drone lidar quantifying aboveground carbon density and gap size-frequency change
accuracy_value: blowdown decreased ACD by at least 17.6%
notes: Structural fingerprint of a single wind event including a change in the gap size distribution.

title: Use of TanDEM-X and SRTM-C Data for Detection of Deforestation Caused by Bark Beetle in Central European Mountains
method: differencing of two global DEMs to detect canopy height loss, validated against a lidar-derived DSM
sensor: TanDEM-X and SRTM-C interferometric DEMs, lidar DSM as reference
host: Central European mountain spruce, Bohemian Forest, Erzgebirge, Giant Mountains
validation_design: lidar-derived digital surface model as reference
accuracy_value: not extracted, reported as vertical bias relative to canopy height
notes: Radar interferometric canopy height, not backscatter, used to detect insect-caused deforestation. A distinct radar route to a structural signal.

title: Stand Delineation of Pinus sylvestris L. Plantations Suffering Decline Processes Based on Biophysical Tree Crown Variables: A Necessary Tool for Adaptive Silviculture
method: random forest with Gini selection over vegetation indices and ALS metrics to map crown pigment and leaf area index, then stand delineation
agent: pests and drought causing defoliation and mortality
accuracy_value: chlorophyll a and b significantly higher in non-defoliated and moderately defoliated trees
notes: Structure and spectra combined for a defoliation gradient. Agents are named jointly and not separated.

title: Analysis of Forest Stand Resistance to Insect Attack According to Remote Sensing Data
method: spectral transfer function of NDVI response to land surface temperature as a resistance indicator
sensor: TERRA and AQUA MODIS NDVI and land surface temperature
validation_design: adjacent intact fir stands as comparison
notes: Damaged and intact stands of one host compared, one insect agent.

title: Prediction of butt rot volume in Norway spruce forest stands using harvester, remotely sensed and environmental data
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: random forest models with pre-harvest and post-harvest predictor sets over 186,026 harvested stems
sensor: remote sensing derived height, environmental and climate data, harvester records
validation_design: two predictor scenarios, theoretical and mapping case
accuracy_value: remote sensing-based height and harvested volume among the most important predictors
notes: Uses an operational record as the label source at stand support, a close design analogue to using aerial overview survey polygons.

title: Elevation and Distribution of Freshwater and Sewage Canals Regulate Canopy Structure and Differentiate Hurricane Damages to a Basin Mangrove Forest
method: spatial regression of hurricane-induced canopy height reduction on pre-hurricane structure and hydrological setting
notes: Structure both predicts and records damage from one agent.

title: Contribution of woody elements to tree level reflectance in boreal forests
method: spectral mixture analysis with a physically-based forest reflectance model, using measured bark, needle and leaf spectra
sensor: airborne hyperspectral, airborne laser scanning, field spectroscopy
agent: insect defoliation, discussed as an application
host: Scots pine, Norway spruce and birch plots, Finland
notes: Quantifies how much of a crown's reflectance comes from woody rather than foliar elements, which bounds how far a spectral defoliation signal can be pushed.

title: Guided Nonlocal Means Estimation of Polarimetric Covariance for Canopy State Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
method: guided nonlocal means estimation of polarimetric covariance matrices at single-look complex resolution
sensor: polarimetric SAR with a coregistered optical image as guide
agent: defoliation and tree death, agent not named
accuracy_value: improved separation of live from defoliated and dead forest
notes: Radar canopy state classification into live, defoliated and dead. Three condition classes, no agent labels.

title: Application of Sentinel-1 radar data for mapping ice disturbance in a forested area
method: eXtreme Gradient Boosting on four combinations of backscatter, polarimetric descriptors, interferometric coherence and optical variables
sensor: Sentinel-1 SAR, optical imagery, orthophoto reference
validation_design: three types of field-based reference data plus manual delineation from pre and post-event orthophotos
accuracy_metric: under and over-estimation of damage class area
accuracy_value: uprooted trees identified with 1 to 11% underestimation; crown loss with 55 to 58% overestimation
notes: Sharpest available result on what radar can and cannot resolve within one agent: uprooting yes, crown loss no. Directly bears on whether a radar predictor could separate defoliation-type from mortality-type damage.

title: Identification of Bark Beetle Infestation in Part of Bohemian Forest using Sentinel-1 Time Series Insar
venue: 2021 IEEE International India Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (InGARSS)
method: time series SAR interferometric coherence compared between infested and non-infested forest
accuracy_value: lower coherence in infested regions, no accuracy figure
notes: Two-page conference paper. Directional result only.

title: Mind the gap: New insights on large-scale forest dynamics over Amazonian forests from airborne lidar and canopy gap data
method: multi-temporal airborne lidar with a link between canopy gaps and canopy mortality
notes: Conference abstract. States that detection and attribution of tree mortality by remote sensing has developed in temperate forests but not tropical ones.

title: Tracking tree mortality across sites with repeat LiDAR data
method: canopy height maps from repeat lidar to detect structural change and large-tree mortality
validation_design: explicitly identified as a challenge, standing dead trees may be missed
notes: Conference abstract. Names validation of repeat-lidar mortality as an unsolved problem.

title: Monitoring Bark Beetle Forest Damage in Central Europe. A Remote Sensing Approach Validated with Field Data
method: two change-detection models for damage and severity, requiring a prior forest mask and dominant species map
notes: Requires a species mask before damage mapping, the same sequencing this project needs to hold host constant.

title: Earth Observation Based Monitoring of Forests in Germany: A Review
method: review of Earth observation based forest monitoring in Germany
agent: storm, drought, heat, bark beetle mass reproduction
notes: Frames drought and bark beetle as a cascade rather than as competing agents.

title: Aboveground carbon loss associated with the spread of ghost forests as sea levels rise
method: repeat lidar with multi-temporal satellite imagery and field biomass to map ghost forest spread and carbon change
sensor: repeat airborne lidar, satellite imagery, field biomass
agent: saltwater intrusion from sea level rise
accuracy_value: 15% (167 km2) of unmanaged public land changed from coastal forest to transition ghost forest between 2001 and 2014
notes: Repeat lidar tracks a slow, non-stand-replacing mortality process, the regime an adelgid signal sits in.

title: Application of multidimensional structural characterization to detect and describe moderate forest disturbance
method: lidar-derived canopy structural traits within a machine learning framework to detect and describe structural change by agent
agent: moderate severity fire, ice storm damage, age-related senescence, hemlock woolly adelgid, beech bark disease, chronic acidification
validation_design: no replication among disturbances, stated by the authors as a limitation
accuracy_value: no classification accuracy reported; two of six agents significantly reduced leaf area
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ3. Six named disturbance agents, including two biotic pests, characterised structurally from lidar. Abstract states verbatim that fire and ice storms primarily affected the amount and position of vegetation within canopies, while acidification, senescence, pathogen, and insect infestation altered canopy arrangement and complexity, and that findings are limited in their generalizability due to lack of replication among disturbances. Each agent sits on a different host, and no classifier accuracy is reported, so it is a descriptive multi-agent structural comparison rather than an attribution model. The 2019 preprint of the same study, doi 10.20944/preprints201911.0082.v1, is titled 'Multidimensional Structural Characterization is Required to Detect and Differentiate Among Moderate Disturbance Agents' and its abstract states verbatim that the authors used lidar-derived canopy structural measured within a machine learning framework to detect and differentiate among various disturbance agents, and that standard disturbance detection methods, such as optical based remote sensing platforms, may currently be limited in their ability to detect, differentiate, and characterize disturbance.

title: A multi-sensor, multi-scale approach to mapping tree mortality in woodland ecosystems
method: multi-scale fusion, UAV imagery for tree-level mortality, airborne lidar for crown mapping and percent canopy mortality, Landsat for regional upscaling
sensor: UAV centimetre imagery, airborne lidar, Landsat
agent: drought, invasive insect outbreaks, pathogens, not separated
accuracy_value: 39% of pinon-juniper in the region showed some level of mortality, patches exceeding 50%
notes: Same region and label environment as Campbell et al. 2023. States that the explanatory power of the mortality driver model was low.

title: CLASSIFICATION OF TREE SPECIES AND STANDING DEAD TREES BY FUSING UAV-BASED LIDAR DATA AND MULTISPECTRAL IMAGERY IN THE 3D DEEP NEURAL NETWORK POINTNET++
venue: ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
method: PointNet++ 3D deep neural network on fused lidar geometry, echo pulse width and multispectral features
agent: pest infestation causing standing dead trees
notes: Standing dead trees classified alongside species from fused structure and spectra.

title: Influence of selected habitat and stand factors on bark beetle Ips typographus (L.) outbreak in the Białowieża Forest
method: individual dead tree detection from ALS and multispectral imagery, then analysis of habitat and stand factors on infestation
sensor: airborne laser scanning, multispectral imagery, digital forest maps
notes: Large-area individual-tree detection using lidar plus spectra, then stand-factor modelling of which trees were attacked.

title: Mapping forest windthrows using high spatial resolution multispectral satellite images
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: comparison of two multispectral constellations for windthrow mapping across acquisition timings
notes: Notes that wind damage acts indirectly through secondary insect outbreaks and fires, a compound-agent problem.

title: Satellite open data to monitor forest damage caused by extreme climate-induced events: a case study of the Vaia storm in Northern Italy
venue: Forestry: An International Journal of Forest Research
method: classification of storm damage from optical and radar open data
accuracy_value: up to 86 percent with Sentinel-2; optical use hampered by persistent cloud
notes: Optical wins on accuracy but loses on availability, the standard trade-off that motivates radar.

title: Continuous Forest Monitoring Using Cumulative Sums of Sentinel-1 Timeseries
method: cumulative sums applied to Sentinel-1 time series for continuous change detection
agent: forest degradation and destruction, agent not identified
notes: Radar analogue of the optical continuous change detection family.

title: Detecting Change in Forest Structure with Simulated GEDI Lidar Waveforms: A Case Study of the Hemlock Woolly Adelgid (HWA; Adelges tsugae) Infestation
method: GEDI waveforms simulated from two airborne lidar acquisitions, waveform metric change regressed on field hemlock mortality
sensor: airborne lidar (NASA G-LiHT and NEON AOP), simulated GEDI spaceborne lidar
host: eastern hemlock (Tsuga canadensis), Harvard Forest ForestGEO
validation_design: field-derived hemlock mortality as reference; robustness tested with added noise and sparse coverage
accuracy_metric: variance explained in a logistic regression
accuracy_value: changes in midstory plant area (PAI 11 to 12 m) and canopy permeability (RH10) accounted for 60% of the variation in hemlock mortality
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ1 AND RQ3. The abstract states verbatim that the insect often causes its host species to defoliate in the midstory and understory before showing impacts in the overstory, and that active sensing can address this by penetrating canopy gaps and recording lower canopy structural changes. This is the published rationale for a structural adelgid signal, on the eastern adelgid, and it is not in references.bib.

title: Urban Tree Health Classification Across Tree Species by Combining Airborne Laser Scanning and Imaging Spectroscopy
method: random forest classification of field-assessed defoliation and discoloration classes from fused structure and spectra, several scenarios compared
agent: declining tree health, agent not identified
notes: Tests whether structure adds to spectra for health classification across heterogeneous species, the same ablation this project plans.

title: eDaRT: The Ecosystem Disturbance and Recovery Tracker system for monitoring landscape disturbances and their cumulative effects
method: automated Landsat-based disturbance and recovery tracking system, operational since 2012
host: USDA Forest Service Pacific Southwest Region
notes: An operational agency system, the class of prior art a management-facing claim has to sit against.

title: Bark beetles as lidar targets and prospects of photonic surveillance
method: laboratory characterisation of beetle light scattering, wing thickness and wingbeat frequency, then field entomological lidar with a controlled release
notes: Lidar detects the insect itself rather than the damage, and the abstract states that the measured parameters can infer target identity in lidar data. A different route to agent identity from canopy structure.

title: Postfire Tree Structure from High-Resolution LiDAR and RBR Sentinel 2A Fire Severity Metrics in a Pinus halepensis-Dominated Burned Stand
method: UAV lidar tree structure measured six months post-fire, compared against a Sentinel-2 relativized burn ratio severity metric
notes: States the core structural argument, that optical sensors have limited ability to penetrate the canopy down to the ground and lidar can overcome this.

title: Reply to “Height-related changes in forest composition explain increasing tree mortality with height during an extreme drought”
method: re-analysis of tree-level mortality for about 1.8 million trees, controlling for forest type and topographic position
sensor: airborne remote sensing derived tree heights and mortality
validation_design: stratified re-analysis across ten topographic positions and ten forest types
accuracy_value: consistent upward trend in mortality rate with increasing tree height in all strata
notes: Structure predicts which trees die under one agent, at very large sample size. Also warns that plot-based sampling undersamples tall trees.

title: Allometry and structural volume change of standing dead southern pine trees using non-destructive terrestrial LiDAR
method: non-destructive terrestrial lidar quantification of standing dead tree structural volume by decay class
notes: Structural decay trajectory of dead trees, which determines how long a mortality signal persists in a structural predictor.

title: Stress Detection in New Zealand Kauri Canopies with WorldView-2 Satellite and LiDAR Data
method: crown-level stress grading from pan-sharpened satellite multispectral with lidar crown height model for crown delineation
validation_design: fieldwork and aerial image interpretation of 1089 crowns
accuracy_metric: effect of crown size on classification
accuracy_value: excluding crowns under 4 m diameter increased performance; crowns under 4 m caused most outliers at 1.8 m pixel size
notes: Quantifies how crown size relative to pixel size limits stress detection, directly relevant to small adelgid polygons.

title: A Deep Learning Approach for Calamity Assessment Using Sentinel-2 Data
method: convolutional neural networks with GIS for calamity assessment against forest department storm damage labels
agent: storm (Friedericke, January 2018), with subsequent bark beetle degradation noted
validation_design: labels provided by the state forest service
notes: Uses an agency damage layer as ground truth, the same label-provenance issue this project carries.

title: Ash Presence and Abundance Derived from Composite Landsat and Sentinel-2 Time Series and Lidar Surface Models in Minnesota, USA
method: Landsat and Sentinel-2 phenological time series with lidar-derived topographic position to classify host species presence and abundance
agent: emerald ash borer (Agrilus planipennis), as the threat motivating host mapping
notes: Lidar topographic position improves host mapping rather than damage mapping.

title: SPATIAL PROCESSING OF SENTINEL IMAGERY FOR MONITORING OF ACACIA FOREST DEGRADATION IN LAKE NAKURU RIPARIAN RESERVE
venue: ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
method: correlation of optical vegetation indices with radar backscatter indices for degradation classification
sensor: Sentinel-1 GRD dual polarised, Sentinel-2 MSI
notes: Optical and radar treated as correlated rather than complementary.

title: Polarimetric Guided Nonlocal Means Covariance Matrix Estimation for Defoliation Mapping
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: guided nonlocal means polarimetric covariance estimation preserving single-look complex resolution, then random forest classification
sensor: RADARSAT-2 quad-polarimetric SAR, aerial photographs for reference
agent: defoliation and tree death in the tundra-forest ecotone
host: tundra-forest ecotone trees, species not stated
validation_design: four live-forest and four dead-tree areas identified from aerial photographs
notes: Highest reported radar accuracy in the set for a live versus dead canopy state, on sparse trees with strong ground contrast. Not an agent classification and the class geometry is extreme.

title: Mapping forest natural disturbances dynamics in the Aosta Valley (Italy) through long-term trends derived from Landsat time series and innovative statistical approaches
method: long-term Landsat time series trends with geometric median annual composites and spectral index trajectories, agents assigned
sensor: Landsat TM, ETM+ and OLI, 1985 to 2019
agent: wildfires, windthrows, snow avalanches, landslides and insect outbreaks
notes: Conference abstract. Five-agent optical attribution, but the agents differ in season, spatial pattern and terrain position.

title: A Convolutional Neural Network Classifier Identifies Tree Species in Mixed-Conifer Forest from Hyperspectral Imagery
method: pixel-based convolutional neural network on hyperspectral imagery with three-dimensional structural information from lidar
host: seven conifer species plus dead standing trees, Sierra Nevada
validation_design: spatially explicit transects and plots split into training, validation and testing
notes: Includes a spatially explicit train, validate and test split, an unusually careful design in this set.

title: Massive tree mortality from flood pulse disturbances in Amazonian floodplain forests: The collateral effects of hydropower production.
method: object-based image analysis with random forest supervised classification of 56 SAR scenes at different flood levels
agent: flood pulse alteration from hydropower damming
host: igapo black-water floodplain forest, Central Amazon
notes: One of the few radar mortality mapping studies with a stated overall accuracy. L-band, not C-band.

title: Rapid Detection of Windthrows Using Sentinel-1 C-Band SAR Data
method: composite of pre and post-storm terrain-corrected SAR acquisitions then windthrow detection
host: mixed temperate forest, Switzerland and northern Germany
notes: Rapid-response radar windthrow detection, the standard C-band use case.

title: Detecting Forest Changes Using Dense Landsat 8 and Sentinel-1 Time Series Data in Tropical Seasonal Forests
method: random forest predicting per-observation disturbance probability from harmonic regression residuals of optical and radar time series
notes: Hybrid optical and radar time series with a machine learning fusion, the design family this project would sit in.

title: Remote sensing of forest die-off in the Anthropocene: From plant ecophysiology to canopy structure
method: review linking drought-induced changes in plant physiology, chemistry and structure to remote sensing observables
notes: The most relevant review for the mechanism this project proposes, spanning ecophysiology through to canopy structure.

title: Comparison and integration of lidar and photogrammetric point clouds for mapping pre-fire forest structure
method: photogrammetric point cloud from pre-fire imagery combined with a post-fire lidar terrain model, correlation structure between the two sources examined
notes: Practical route to pre-event structure where lidar predates or postdates the disturbance, the exact timing problem a lidar-based attribution design faces.

title: The potential of dual-wavelength terrestrial lidar in early detection of Ips typographus (L.) infestation – Leaf water content as a proxy
method: dual-wavelength terrestrial lidar with leaf water content as a proxy for infestation status
notes: Already cited in the survey as Junttila 2019. Lidar detects a physiological rather than a geometric change, using two wavelengths.

title: Long-Term Impacts of Selective Logging on Amazon Forest Dynamics from Multi-Temporal Airborne LiDAR
method: multi-temporal ALS estimating canopy and understory structural change, plus a binary classifier for intact versus logged
accuracy_value: canopy gap frequency significantly higher in logged forests after 8 years; understory of logged areas could not be distinguished from intact
notes: Explicit finding on which structural strata retain a disturbance signature and which do not.

title: Synthetic aperture radar sensitivity to forest changes: A simulations-based study for the Romanian forests.
method: electromagnetic simulation of C-, L- and P-band SAR response to vegetation water content, leaf area index and disturbance
sensor: simulated C-, L- and P-band SAR
agent: natural and anthropogenic disturbance including defoliation and drought
host: beech, oak and coniferous forest, Romania
accuracy_metric: modulation of the SAR signal in dB
accuracy_value: C-band largely influenced by foliage volume and therefore possibly useful for monitoring defoliation; water content changes modulated the C-band signal by less than 1 dB, which may be insufficient for meaningful retrieval
notes: The strongest physical bound in the set on what a C-band predictor can carry. Says defoliation yes, water content no, and separates behaviour by wavelength.

title: Intra-annual Ips typographus outbreak monitoring using a multi-temporal GIS analysis based on hyperspectral and ALS data in the Białowieża Forests
method: multi-temporal GIS workflow mapping dead trees at single-tree level from hyperspectral and ALS, with timber loss estimation
sensor: airborne hyperspectral, airborne laser scanning, field inventory
notes: Intra-annual outbreak tracking at tree level from fused structure and spectra.

title: Mapping forest successional stages in the Brazilian Amazon using forest heights derived from TanDEM-X SAR interferometry
method: forest top height from interferometric SAR used to discriminate successional stages
notes: Radar-derived height, not backscatter, discriminates disturbance-history classes. The nearest radar analogue to a structural attribution predictor.

title: Combined use of spectral and structural characteristics for improved red band needle blight detection in pine plantation stands
method: comparison of spectral signatures and individual-tree lidar metrics, singly and combined, for infection detection
sensor: hyperspectral imagery, airborne lidar, leaf spectroscopy
accuracy_value: good separation between the two pine stands using several spectral indices; combined result not extracted from abstract
notes: Explicitly tests whether adding structural metrics to spectra improves detection of a single pathogen on one host. The design is the ablation this project plans, with one agent instead of two.

title: Radar Satellite Imagery for Detecting Bark Beetle Outbreaks in Forests
method: structured review of radar for bark beetle detection with a theoretical account of radar-canopy interaction
notes: Already cited as Hollaus 2019. Verbatim conclusions worth quoting: mono-temporal radar data are of limited use; shorter wavelength (e.g. C-band; X-band) have a higher potential than longer wavelength such as L-band; optimal acquisition is April to June pre-event and August to October post-event.

title: Assessing Legacy Effects of Wildfires on the Crown Structure of Fire-Tolerant Eucalypt Trees Using Airborne LiDAR Data
method: individual tree crown metrics from airborne lidar across four wildfire severity classes, validated with field measurements
support: individual tree crown, 51 plots of 0.05 ha
validation_design: field-validated across unburnt, low, moderate and high severity
class_balance_reported: yes, four severity types across 51 plots
accuracy_value: significant differences in field-assessed and lidar crown attributes across severity types
notes: Structural legacy still detectable 8.5 years after the event, which sets a persistence expectation for a structural signal.

title: Estimating prescribed fire impacts and post-fire tree survival in eucalyptus forests of Western Australia with L-band SAR data
method: multi-temporal Radar Burn Ratio relating backscatter change to burn outcome and post-fire tree survival
notes: Radar index tuned to understorey and surface fuel change, a lower-canopy signal that optical sensors miss.

title: Integration of WorldView-2 and airborne laser scanning data to classify defoliation levels in Quercus ilex L. Dehesas affected by root rot mortality: Management implications
method: random forest on combined WorldView-2 bands, vegetation indices and ALS structural metrics to classify two defoliation levels at a 30% crown threshold
accuracy_value: seven predictors selected from ALS metrics, WorldView-2 bands and indices
notes: An ALS height percentile was retained alongside spectral predictors for defoliation classification in a low-density open canopy, the structural setting most like an open fir stand.

title: Forest dieback processes in the Central European Mountains in the context of terrain topography and selected stand attributes
method: lidar and aerial imagery with terrain and stand attributes to characterise dieback patterns
agent: climate change, insect pests or pollution, explicitly not separated
notes: States plainly that dieback is characterised by high variability and is independent of whether it is caused by climate, insects or pollution, which is the null this project is testing against.

title: Boreal Forest Snow Damage Mapping Using Multi-Temporal Sentinel-1 Data
method: improved k nearest neighbour, logistic regression and support vector machine on Sentinel-1 time series
validation_design: official snow damage recordings from a large event
notes: Radar mapping of one of the least-studied abiotic agents, using an operational damage record as reference.

title: A new method of equiangular sectorial voxelization of single-scan terrestrial laser scanning data and its applications in forest defoliation estimation
venue: Isprs Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
method: equiangular sectorial voxelization of single-scan TLS with point density metrics regressed on defoliation
accuracy_value: R squared 0.89, RMSE 12 percent of defoliation
notes: Among the strongest structure-to-defoliation relationships in the set, from a single scan with no multitemporal requirement.

title: Tree defoliation classification based on point distribution features derived from single-scan terrestrial laser scanning data
method: sixty point-distribution features from single-scan TLS classified into three defoliation classes at tree and plot scale
accuracy_value: three classes: healthy or slightly, moderately, and severely defoliated
notes: Structure alone grades insect defoliation severity from a single date, which removes the need for a pre-disturbance acquisition.

title: Structural development following stand-replacing disturbance in a boreal mixedwood forest
method: about 7000 ALS-derived stem size distributions over a 50-year disturbance chronosequence, compared by disturbance type and species group
agent: stand-replacing disturbance types, including harvest and fire
notes: Compares structural development pathways between disturbance types at large sample size. It describes differences, it does not classify agent.

title: Monitoring Broadleaf Forest Pest Based on L-Band SAR Tomography
venue: IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environment
method: simulation of L-band tomographic SAR echoes for normal and pest-affected forest, then 3D structure extraction
accuracy_value: differences between normal and pest forest demonstrated qualitatively
notes: Explicitly proposes monitoring forest pest by extracting 3D structural information from radar tomography. The idea exists; the demonstration is simulated only.

title: Assessing Post-Fire Tree Mortality and Biomass Change by Integrating Lidar and Hyperspectral data
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
method: fusion of lidar and hyperspectral with field observations across a burn severity gradient
host: Pine Barrens mixed forest, eastern USA
validation_design: field observations across a burn gradient
notes: Structure and spectra fused for mortality and biomass change under one agent.

title: Utilizing multispectral lidar in the detection of declined trees
method: multispectral terrestrial lidar for detection and assessment of tree decline caused by different stressors
agent: multiple stressors, insects and pathogens and heat
notes: Doctoral thesis. Explicitly frames multispectral lidar as giving three-dimensional and spectral information simultaneously for decline caused by different stressors. Flagged for full-text check on whether stressors are separated.

title: Three decades of forest structural dynamics over Canada's forested ecosystems using Landsat time-series and lidar plots
method: lidar plot data combined with Landsat pixel composites to produce annual structure maps over three decades
sensor: airborne lidar transect plots, Landsat time series
validation_design: lidar plots as calibration and validation
notes: The national Canadian structure product a British Columbia design would sit against.

title: Fire, fragmentation, and windstorms: A recipe for tropical forest degradation
method: pre and post-windstorm field mortality with airborne lidar tree heights and canopy gap metrics across a replicated burn experiment
agent: windstorm, fire, and edge effects, interacting
host: southeastern Amazonian forest, three 50 ha plots
support: plot, individual tree over 10 cm DBH
validation_design: replicated fire experiment with control and two burn frequencies
accuracy_metric: mortality rate and mode of death
accuracy_value: greater windstorm damage in burned plots than control, exact figures not extracted from abstract
notes: Rare experimental test of interaction between two disturbance agents on the same forest. Agents are wind and fire, both abiotic.

title: Quantifying long-term changes in carbon stocks and forest structure from Amazon forest degradation
method: annual Landsat time series combined with high-density airborne lidar to quantify carbon and structural change by degradation type
accuracy_value: degraded forests contained 45.1% of the carbon stocks of intact forests, with differences persisting after 15 years of regrowth
notes: Compares logging against fire as degradation pathways with different structural consequences.

title: Measuring short-term post-fire forest recovery across a burn severity gradient in a mixed pine-oak forest using multi-sensor remote sensing techniques
method: 1 m simultaneous airborne imaging spectroscopy and lidar with 2 m satellite imagery to separate canopy from understory recovery
sensor: airborne imaging spectroscopy and lidar at 1 m, satellite multispectral at 2 m
agent: wildfire, across a burn severity gradient
notes: Uses structure specifically to remove understory contamination from a spectral recovery signal, a confound that also afflicts open fir stands.

title: Urban tree health assessment using airborne hyperspectral and LiDAR imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: lidar-based tree detection and segmentation then PLSR models of chlorophyll and leaf area index from canopy spectra, with structural metrics
agent: declining tree health, agent not identified
accuracy_metric: segmentation accuracy, RMSE and R squared
accuracy_value: tree delineation average accuracy 91%; chlorophyll RMSE 2.8 micrograms per cm2 R2 0.77; LAI RMSE 0.5 R2 0.66
notes: Well-reported fusion workflow with explicit accuracies at each step.

title: The extent of mangrove change and potential for recovery following severe Tropical Cyclone Yasi, Hinchinbrook Island, Queensland, Australia
method: foliage projective cover from Landsat with aerial and RapidEye imagery to map severe windthrow and recovery
notes: Damage varied by dominant species and structure, which is a host-effect confound of the type this design removes.

title: Detection of windthrows and insect outbreaks by L-band SAR: A case study in the Bavarian Forest National Park
method: change detection on L-band spaceborne SAR backscatter, applied separately to wind-damaged and insect-damaged areas
host: Bavarian Forest National Park, Norway spruce dominated
validation_design: not stated in abstract; accuracy ranges given by acquisition date and environmental condition
accuracy_value: wind damage 69 to 84%; insect outbreaks 65 to 88%; susceptible or initial green-attack areas 64 to 74%
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ3, already cited as Tanase 2018. Two agents in one park on one dominant host, but the abstract reports delineation of each agent's areas separately rather than a classifier that decides between them, and one agent is abiotic. It is the closest published approach to the target design and its green-attack accuracy of 64 to 74% is the realistic ceiling for early insect detection from radar.

title: Mapping canopy defoliation by herbivorous insects at the individual tree level using bi-temporal airborne imaging spectroscopy and LiDAR measurements
method: bi-temporal airborne imaging spectroscopy and lidar at 1 m, ordinary least squares models fitted from each sensor alone and combined
host: mixed oak-pine forest, Long Island, New York
validation_design: bi-temporal, model comparison; split design not stated in abstract
accuracy_metric: adjusted R squared and RMSE for defoliation severity
accuracy_value: lidar only adj. R2 0.77 RMSE 15.37%; imaging spectroscopy only adj. R2 0.63 RMSE 19.11%; combined adj. R2 0.81 RMSE 14.46%
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ3. The lidar-only model outperformed the hyperspectral-only model for mapping insect defoliation at individual tree level, and the combination beat both. This establishes that structure carries insect damage information at least as well as spectra, so that part of the project's hypothesis is supported rather than novel. Named lidar metrics were B70, intensity skewness and kurtosis.

title: Characterizing Tropical Forest Cover Loss Using Dense Sentinel-1 Data and Active Fire Alerts
method: near real-time radar forest cover loss combined with active fire alerts, separating fires that predate, coincide with and postdate loss
sensor: Sentinel-1 C-band SAR, VIIRS active fire alerts
agent: fire versus other causes of forest cover loss
host: natural and plantation forest, Riau, Indonesia
support: medium spatial scale, high temporal detail
notes: Attribution of loss to fire by relative timing rather than by signal shape. A useful precedent for using an independent agent-specific data stream as the attribution key.

title: Ensemble classification of individual Pinus crowns from multispectral satellite imagery and airborne LiDAR
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: ensemble classification of individual crowns under three schemes: lidar alone, WorldView-2 alone, and both combined
sensor: high-density airborne lidar at 160 returns per m2, WorldView-2
host: Pinus sylvestris and Pinus uncinata, Barcelonnette
notes: Closest available test of whether crown structure separates two congeneric conifers. Relevant because this project must hold host constant and needs to know how much structure varies by species alone.

title: Impacts of Water Stress on Forest Recovery and Its Interaction with Canopy Height
venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
method: regional analysis of post-drought recovery paths stratified by lidar-derived canopy height and water availability
sensor: lidar-derived canopy height, satellite vegetation records
notes: Canopy height modifies the recovery signal after an agent, so structure is a covariate of damage response as well as a predictor of it.

title: Fusion of NASA Airborne Snow Observatory (ASO) Lidar Time Series over Mountain Forest Landscapes
method: coherent merging of weekly snow-survey lidar acquisitions to build a dense multi-year point cloud time series
agent: fire, insect damage and drought, named as targets
accuracy_value: weekly acquisitions at about 1 point per m2 merged to about 12 points per m2
notes: Shows how repeat lidar can be assembled opportunistically from acquisitions flown for another purpose, which is the situation with provincial lidar coverage.

title: Classification for non infected and infected ganoderma boninense of oil palm trees using ALOS PALSAR-2 backscattering coefficient
venue: IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environment
method: decision tree classification of infected versus non-infected trees from HH and HV backscatter
notes: Radar backscatter alone used to classify infection status of a single host. Plantation, and the disease attacks the stem base rather than the canopy.

title: Assessing the Trade-Offs of SPOT7 Imagery for Monitoring Natural Forest Canopy Intactness
method: comparison of canopy gap detection accuracy between two pan-sharpening resolutions, with NDVI and SAR tested as accuracy enhancers
sensor: SPOT7 at 5 m and 1.5 m, SAR
notes: Tests whether adding radar improves an optical gap product.

title: Current remote sensing approaches to monitoring forest degradation in support of countries measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) systems for REDD+
method: review of degradation monitoring approaches, split between canopy cover change detection and biomass loss quantification
notes: States that no single method can monitor degradation because the answer depends on the degradation type and the observation window.

title: Remote sensing of forest insect disturbances: Current state and future directions
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: systematic review grouping studies into bark beetles, broadleaved defoliators and coniferous defoliators, comparing sensors and methods within and across types
notes: CENTRAL RECORD. Senf et al. 2017. Its first stated future research direction is verbatim 'Separate insect disturbances from other agents', which is an explicit statement that the separation problem was open at that date. It also finds substantial differences between methods used for mapping bark beetles and defoliators. Not in references.bib.

title: Monitoring of Forest Structure Dynamics by Means of L-Band SAR Tomography
method: compressive sensing tomographic reconstruction of 3D reflectivity profiles, with horizontal and vertical structure indices from local maxima
sensor: L-band tomographic SAR, simulated and experimental
notes: Radar tomography producing explicit horizontal and vertical structure indices, the closest radar analogue to lidar structural metrics.

title: Using Intra-Annual Landsat Time Series for Attributing Forest Disturbance Agents in Central Europe
method: breakpoint detection on all available Landsat observations 1984 to 2016, then classification of four disturbance classes from spectral, temporal and topographic metrics
agent: windthrow, cleared windthrow, bark beetles, other harvest
host: Central European forest, three sites, managed and protected
validation_design: three sites, design not further stated in abstract
notes: Seed study, cited as Oeser 2017. Two of the four classes are the same agent in different management states. The abstract states verbatim that temporal proximity to storm events was among the most important predictors and that elevation information was very effective for discriminating disturbance agents, so a substantial part of the discrimination comes from site and timing rather than from the damage signature itself.

title: Individual Tree Crown Delineation from Airborne Laser Scanning for Diseased Larch Forest Stands
method: comparison of marker-controlled watershed and region growing crown segmentation across infection levels
sensor: airborne laser scanning canopy height models
validation_design: sample plots at two sites across a range of infection levels
notes: Shows that disease-induced canopy irregularity degrades the crown segmentation that a tree-level structural analysis depends on. A methodological warning for this project.

title: Prediction of Forest Canopy and Surface Fuels from Lidar and Satellite Time Series Data in a Bark Beetle-Affected Forest
method: random forest predicting field-measured canopy and surface fuels from lidar and Landsat time series, with correlation against mortality severity
agent: mountain pine beetle (Dendroctonus ponderosae), six years post-outbreak
accuracy_value: 59% available canopy fuel, 48% canopy bulk density, 35% canopy base height, 70% for the fourth attribute
notes: Quantifies how much structural variation lidar plus optical explains six years after an insect outbreak, which is a realistic expectation for a lagged structural signal.

title: Episodic Canopy Structural Transformations and Biological Invasion in a Hawaiian Forest
method: multi-temporal high-resolution lidar quantifying near-decadal net change in canopy height and gap distribution
agent: drought, host-specific insect outbreak (Scotorythra paludicola), invasive species
host: Hawaiian sub-montane native forest, Mauna Kea
accuracy_value: net loss in average canopy height, exact value not extracted from abstract
notes: Three interacting drivers including a host-specific insect, observed structurally. The drivers are described together, not separated.

title: Measuring leaf water content using multispectral terrestrial laser scanning
method: multispectral terrestrial laser scanning intensity ratios regressed on measured leaf water content
sensor: multispectral terrestrial laser scanning at 690, 905 and 1550 nm
agent: tree stress preceding drought, insect and pathogen damage
accuracy_value: a ratio of 905 nm and 1550 nm explained 84% of variation in leaf water content, prediction accuracy 0.0041 g per cm2
notes: Establishes the physical mechanism behind dual-wavelength lidar stress detection under controlled conditions.

title: Remote sensing of seasonal changes and disturbances in mangrove forest: a case study from South Florida
method: four vegetation indices from 150 Landsat scenes with lidar, separating seasonal variation from episodic disturbance
accuracy_value: normalized difference moisture index performed best; chilling and hurricane damage showed distinct spatial patterns
notes: Two abiotic agents on one forest type distinguished by spatial pattern rather than by spectral signature, and separated from a seasonal cycle. The spatial-pattern route is a viable alternative to a signature-based route.

title: Forest Disturbances and Regrowth Assessment Using ALOS PALSAR Data from 2007 to 2010 in Vietnam, Cambodia and Lao PDR
method: expectation maximisation change detection on L-band SAR mosaics for disturbance and regrowth
host: tropical forest, Vietnam, Cambodia, Lao PDR
validation_design: training and testing database, described as reliable
notes: L-band chosen because intensity is sensitive to biomass loss, the opposite trade-off from C-band foliage sensitivity.

title: Post-Fire Changes in Forest Biomass Retrieved by Airborne LiDAR in Amazonia
method: airborne lidar quantification of post-fire canopy height and biomass change with 25 inventory plots
notes: Fire histories five years apart give a structural recovery gradient from a single agent.

title: The Impact of Fine-Scale Disturbances on the Predictability of Vegetation Dynamics and Carbon Flux
method: repeat lidar used to test the effect of fine-scale disturbance on the predictability of vegetation dynamics and carbon flux
agent: fine-scale disturbance, plus cyclones, fire and pest outbreaks as contrast
notes: Argues that small frequent disturbances may matter as much as large extreme events, which is the severity regime of the adelgid record.

title: Remote Sensing of Tamarisk Biomass, Insect Herbivory, and Defoliation: Novel Methods in the Grand Canyon Region, Arizona
method: classification of host distribution and beetle defoliation from 0.2 m airborne multispectral, with lidar biomass estimation
sensor: airborne multispectral at 0.2 m, airborne lidar at 100 points per m2
agent: northern tamarisk beetle (Diorhabda carinulata), a deliberately introduced biocontrol agent
accuracy_value: 86 percent; mean leaf biomass loss 0.52 kg per m2, 25,692 kg across the study area
notes: Combines a spectral defoliation map with a lidar biomass model to convert defoliation into mass loss.

title: Development of monitoring methods for Hemlock Woolly Adelgid induced tree mortality within a Southern Appalachian landscape with inhibited access
method: semi-automatic mapping of conifer patches including living hemlock and adelgid-caused mortality from aerial data
sensor: aerial imagery, further sensors not stated in abstract
host: eastern hemlock (Tsuga canadensis) and Carolina hemlock (Tsuga caroliniana)
notes: Directly relevant to RQ1. Emphasises that the landscape carries several other conifer species, so the host must be isolated before the agent can be mapped, the same sequencing this project requires.

title: Mapping dynamics of deforestation and forest degradation in tropical forests using radar satellite data
method: detection algorithm on L-band backscatter allowing repeated disturbance on the same land and separating slow from fast recovery
agent: deforestation, degradation from selective logging, successional dynamics
host: tropical forest, Madre de Dios, Peru
accuracy_metric: area disturbed and false positive rate
accuracy_value: 2.3% of land disturbed over three years with a false positive rate of 0.3% of area; low but significant detection rate for sparse small-scale selective logging
notes: One of the few radar studies that reports a false positive rate as area, which is the honest way to report a rare-class detector.
